open_points.subject: operation-element conclusion
open_points.text: “runs reads … an operation element's conclusion (A11 rule 3) through effects.operation_element_conclusion” conflicts with “NodeExecution M23 is written … by runs for every other record — an operation element concluded contract_violation on a misfit input before effects is called included” and “a module … never decides from another module's raw records.”
open_points.question: Who owns the conclusion of an operation element whose NodeExecution was written by runs before effects was called, and how may effects obtain that record without depending on runs?
options: runs interprets runs-written operation records and calls effects only for EffectAttempt-dependent conclusions
runs passes the relevant NodeExecution into effects.operation_element_conclusion
effects reads runs-owned NodeExecutions directly from store
effects writes or owns every operation-element NodeExecution
open_points.default_guess: runs interprets ordinary runs-written conclusions and uses effects only to overlay EffectAttempt resolution on effect-owned attempts

open_points.subject: manifest instance validation
open_points.text: “bindings” owns “proposal checks in their fixed order,” including instance URL and required-header validity, while “service_invoker” owns “the pre-send checks of the instance” for the same URL, repeated-header and invalid-header rules; only check_request_shape is named as a validation capability offered to bindings.
open_points.question: Which module owns the reusable validation of api_base_url and required_headers that must run both when proposing or accepting a binding and before sending?
options: service_invoker owns pure instance-validation capabilities consumed by bindings
bindings owns instance validation and returns a validated instance object consumed by service_invoker
both modules implement the same validation rules independently
open_points.default_guess: service_invoker owns pure instance-validation capabilities and bindings delegates to them

open_points.subject: unknown-reference checks
open_points.text: “surface … gives the ‘unknown reference’ refusal” and “must not own any operation's own checks,” while raw store reads are allowed only for “returning records as they are for inspection and traces”; several owning modules, especially effects, name no public read capability by which surface can check approval, grant or attempt existence.
open_points.question: Does surface perform record-existence checks, or does each owning module detect an unknown reference and return a common refusal for surface to expose?
options: each owning module checks references and returns a common unknown-reference result
every owning module exposes an existence/read capability used by surface
surface may query store directly for existence outside inspection
open_points.default_guess: each owning module checks its own references and surface only maps the common result to the protocol refusal
